'''Rachel (Raquel) Chan''' is a pioneering Argentine [[biochemist]] from the [[Santa Fe Province]] in Argentina.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://croplife.org/industry-profile/female-foodheroes-raquel-lia-chan/|title=Female #FoodHeroes: Raquel Lía Chan|website=CropLife International|language=en-US|access-date=2020-03-04}}</ref> Her work has centered on photosynthesis,<ref name=":0" /> and she has invented multiple drought-resistant seeds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ifama.org/resources/files/2014-Conference/979.pdf|title=Bioceres: Ag Biotechnology from Argentina|last=Feeney|first=Roberto|date=2014|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.isaaa.org/kc/cropbiotechupdate/article/default.asp?ID=16811|title=Argentina to Release Drought and Salt Tolerant Soybean|website=Crop Biotech Update|language=en|access-date=2020-03-04}}</ref> She is the Director of the Agrobiotechnology Institute of Santa Fe (IAL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/wipo/posts/1891015850970732|title=World Intellectual Property Organization|website=www.facebook.com|language=en|access-date=2020-03-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.unsam.edu.ar/tss/raquel-chan-no-nos-mandaron-a-lavar-los-platos-pero-estamos-en-ese-camino/|title=Raquel Chan: "No nos mandaron a lavar los platos, pero estamos en ese camino" – Agencia TSS|last=YurkevichResponder|first=Rafael|language=es-ES|access-date=2020-03-04}}</ref> Chan was named one of the ten most outstanding women scientists in [[Latin America]] by the [[BBC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eluniverso.com/vida-estilo/2013/10/18/nota/1598816/ecuatoriana-10-cientificas-mas-destacadas-latinoamerica|title=Ecuatoriana entre las 10 científicas más destacadas de Latinoamérica|author=EL UNIVERSO|work=El Universo|access-date=4 November 2015}}</ref>

==Education==
Chan did her undergraduate study at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].<ref name="elsevier.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.journals.elsevier.com/journal-of-biotechnology/editorial-board/raquel-lia-chan/|title=Raquel Lia Chan|work=Elsevier|access-date=4 November 2015}}</ref> She received her Ph.D. degree in [[Biochemistry]] from the [[National University of Rosario]], Argentina, in 1988.<ref name="elsevier.com"/>

== HB4 technology ==
In 2003, Raquel Chan and Daniel González, in collaboration with the company [[Bioceres]], the [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council|National Scientific and Technical Research Council (CONICET)]] and the [[National University of the Littoral|Universidad Nacional del Litoral (UNL)]], led the team that discovered the effect of tolerance to the drought of a sunflower gene called hahb-4.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-15 |title=Raquel Chan. Quién es y cómo piensa la mujer que busca alimentar al mundo y se merece un Premio Nobel |url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/la-nacion-revista/raquel-chan-quien-es-y-como-piensa-la-mujer-que-busca-alimentar-al-mundo-y-se-merece-un-premio-nobel-nid15012022/ |access-date=2022-09-22 |website=LA NACION |language=es}}</ref>

The initial discovery allowed Bioceres to develop a specific project to generate new hahb-4 transformation events on [[Arabidopsis thaliana]]. The objective of the project was to evaluate different promoters and molecular constructions to be used later on crops of agronomic interest.

In the course of developing the technology a particular efficiency of the hahb-4 gene was identified. This new, modified version of the original gene provides a greater efficiency in [[drought]] conditions. The modified hahb-4 sunflower gene improves adaptation of the plant to the environment, which allows obtaining a higher yield of grain. HB4® is currently the world's only drought-tolerant GMO technology for wheat and soybean crops.

==Career==
Chan holds positions at the National University of Litoral, the [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council|National Research Council (CONICET)]], and the Agrobiotechnology Institute of Santa Fe (IAL).<ref name="elsevier.com"/> The IAL researches [[biotechnology]] and plant [[molecular biology]].<ref name="elsevier.com"/>  Chan's research concentrates on [[photosynthesis]]. After returning to Argentina in 1992, she began a project to understand how plants are affected by environmental conditions.<ref name="elsevier.com"/> Chan's team of scientific researchers created more drought resistant seeds.<ref>{{cite book | last1=Blankstein | first1=A.M. | last2=Noguera | first2=P. | title=Excellence Through Equity: Five Principles of Courageous Leadership to Guide Achievement for Every Student | publisher=SAGE Publications | year=2015 | isbn=978-1-4833-9285-1 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PtW5BgAAQBAJ&pg=PT206 | access-date=2015-11-04}}</ref>

About her work Chan stated, "The creation of more drought-resistant seed was a very long process of basic research with research groups were changing over time. It was a day and Eureka! It was like the discovery of Newton when the apple fell" <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bbc.com/mundo/noticias/2013/10/130930_ciencia_mujeres_cientificas_mr|title=10 mujeres que lideran la ciencia en América Latina|work=BBC Mundo|access-date=4 November 2015}}</ref>

Supporters of the technology say the boost in productivity could mean as much as $10 billion in added profits each year, particularly after a severe drought recently slashed Argentina's soy output by more than a third.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://phys.org/news/2012-04-drought-resistant-argentine-soy.html|title=Drought-resistant Argentine soy raises hopes, concerns|work=phys.org|access-date=4 November 2015}}</ref>

Chan continues to support the South American agricultural innovation, helping commercialize drought-resistant soybean seeds as recently as 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://geneticliteracyproject.org/2018/09/06/argentina-and-gmos-exploring-the-nations-long-relationship-with-biotech-crops/|title=Argentina and GMOs: Exploring the nation's long relationship with biotech crops|last=Cerier|first=Steven|date=2018-09-06|website=Genetic Literacy Project|language=en-US|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-03-04}}</ref>

She was granted the [[Konex Award]] Merit Diploma in 2013 and the Platinum Konex Award in 2023 for her work in Biotechnology.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2023-05-15|author=Fundación Konex|date=2 May 2023|language=es|title=Raquel Chan: Premio Konex 2013 y 2023 - Ciencia y Tecnología|url=https://www.fundacionkonex.org/b4585-raquel-chan|website=fundacionkonex.org}}<!-- auto-translated by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>
